headline: Sheikh Hasina and 33 others indicted in truck driver killing case
summary: A special court in Dhaka has framed charges against the deposed prime minister and several former ministers for the death of Mohammad Hossain during the July uprising.
details: A special court in Dhaka has framed charges against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 33 others in connection with the killing of a truck driver during the July uprising.

The order was passed by Judge Md Rabiul Alam of the Special Judge’s Court-4. Eleven of the accused, including former ICT state minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak and former lawmaker Sadek Khan, pleaded not guilty.
The court has scheduled November 25 for the recording of statements from prosecution witnesses.
Nine accused individuals, including Palak and Sadek, were produced from jail during the hearing, while two others were present in court.
Arrest warrants have been issued for 23 absconding accused, including Sheikh Hasina and former ministers Obaidul Quader, Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Mohammed Hasan Mahmud, and Jahangir Kabir Nanak.
The case stems from the death of 25-year-sold truck driver Mohammad Hossain, who was killed in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area during protests on July 19, 2024.
The victim's mother, Rina Begum, filed the murder case on August 27, accusing Hasina and 15 others, which was later registered as an FIR by Mohammadpur Police Station.
According to court records, 920 cases, including 560 linked to killings, have been filed at various police stations in Dhaka alone up until July this year.

Sheikh Hasina and 33 others have been indicted for the killing of a truck driver during the July uprising.

The order was passed by Judge Md Rabiul Alam of the Special Judge’s Court-4. Eleven of the accused, including former ICT state minister Zunaid Ahmed Palak and former lawmaker Sadek Khan, pleaded not guilty.

The court has scheduled November 25 for the recording of statements from prosecution witnesses.

Nine accused individuals, including Palak and Sadek, were produced from jail during the hearing, while two others were present in court.

Arrest warrants have been issued for 23 absconding accused, including Sheikh Hasina and former ministers Obaidul Quader, Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Mohammed Hasan Mahmud, and Jahangir Kabir Nanak.

The case stems from the death of 25-year-sold truck driver Mohammad Hossain, who was killed in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area during protests on July 19, 2024.

The victim's mother, Rina Begum, filed the murder case on August 27, accusing Hasina and 15 others, which was later registered as an FIR by Mohammadpur Police Station.

According to court records, 920 cases, including 560 linked to killings, have been filed at various police stations in Dhaka alone up until July this year.

headline: Winds up to 117kmph: Cyclone Arnab grows into severe storm
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has issued warning signal No. 3 for four seaports as the storm moves west-northwest.
details: Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining west-central waters. The storm is moving west-northwest, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.
At 6pm on Sunday, the storm's centre was located 870km southwest of Chittagong Port, 810km southwest of Cox’s Bazar, 795km south of Mongla, and 770km south of Payra.
Winds near the centre are blowing continuously at up to 89km per hour within a 64km radius, with gusts reaching 117km per hour. The sea remains rough near the storm’s centre.
The Met Office has asked Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra seaports to maintain local warning signal No. 3.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.
The storm is expected to intensify further into a "very severe" cyclonic storm before crossing India’s Andhra coast on Wednesday.
caption:
Winds of up to 117kmph as Cyclone Arnab intensifies into a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal.

Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the east-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining west-central waters. The storm is moving west-northwest, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.

At 6pm on Sunday, the storm's centre was located 870km southwest of Chittagong Port, 810km southwest of Cox’s Bazar, 795km south of Mongla, and 770km south of Payra.

Winds near the centre are blowing continuously at up to 89km per hour within a 64km radius, with gusts reaching 117km per hour. The sea remains rough near the storm’s centre.

The Met Office has asked Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra seaports to maintain local warning signal No. 3.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast and proceed with caution until further notice.

The storm is expected to intensify further into a "very severe" cyclonic storm before crossing India’s Andhra coast on Wednesday.
